thread:
alice: heads-up: noticing sustained KV cache growth for tenant_jupiter over the last 6h, paging climbs and reuse drops. paging spikes after longctx requests. Anyone else seeing this? :eyes:
kv-bot: alert: kv_pager::high_io triggered for shard-7 (tenant_jupiter) at 1958001200, io_wait 4.2s
ben: yup saw the alert. first thought was noisy longctx sequences pinning large page ranges. can you paste the tail of the eviction log?
alice: paste below — high verbosity from the edge: 
```
[1958001189] tenant=tenant_jupiter pages_in=12503 pages_out=12498 active_pages=28090 fragmentation=0.34 kv_reuse_rate=0.12
[1958001195] tenant=tenant_jupiter pages_in=13045 pages_out=12990 active_pages=28600 fragmentation=0.38 kv_reuse_rate=0.09
[1958001205] tenant=tenant_jupiter pages_in=14210 pages_out=14180 active_pages=30844 fragmentation=0.51 kv_reuse_rate=0.03
```
carlos: fragmentation up to 0.51 is wild. that + reuse_rate drop to 0.03 implies a lot of single-use pages and long tail references. could be longctx that walks a big keyspace once.
dana: did you correlate with kernel selection? we recently rolled kernel v2.3 which changed LRU scan batch size. maybe eviction path is too eager for small slices and ends up scattering pages.
ben: good call. i profiled the eviction thread earlier — sampler showed many callbacks spending time in kernel_select_path("v2.3"->quantized_copy). stack traces looked like: 
```
worker_evict() -> choose_kernel() -> quantized_copy() -> memcpy_slowpath()
```
emma: if quantized_copy is slower we might hold eviction locks longer and cause paging to queue up. but fragmentation suggests allocation pattern issue too (slab reuse failing).
alice: i'm running live heap-sampled dump now with tenant sampling turned on. will share soon. also we observed memory growth correlates with sequence length > 12k tokens. longctx sessions keep positive write patterns.
kv-bot: experiment: tenant_shaper ramp applied to tenant_jupiter at 1958001300, rate=0.5 (kv residency shaper)
carlos: how did shaper compute the weights? is it strictly tokens or page-usage?
dana: prototype uses rolling-window page residency + weighted token tail; idea is to throttle residency delta instead of absolute throughput. code snippet: 
```
if delta_residency > quota * window_factor:
    throttle_residency(tenant, scale=0.5)
```
ben: quick note — throttling residency without addressing fragmentation just shifts the problem to other tenants because freed pages are fragmented and not reusable. we need compaction or better reuse policy.
emma: proposal: 1) enable periodic in-place compaction that attempts to merge adjacent free pages per slab, 2) change eviction heuristic to prefer pages with low reuse_score and high fragmentation impact, 3) sample longctx requests and back-pressure them at route-level.
alice: i like that. can we test a smaller change first: enable compaction on shards reporting frag>0.4 and reuse_rate<0.1, for 10s windows. low-risk toggle.
carlos: +1. also add a metric: post_compaction_reuse_delta and compaction_io_cost. need to ensure compaction doesn't spike latency.
dana: i ran a micro-sim locally — compaction decreased active_pages by ~7% and reuse_rate rose from 0.03 -> 0.09, but IO increased 12% for the compaction window. that's acceptable if we confine compaction to off-peak or use I/O cgroup.
ben: another angle: kernel chooser heuristics — revert the batching size change in v2.3 for eviction threads only. A/B it on a small subset. that should reduce lock hold time in quantized_copy.
emma: i'll wire up a canary: shard-7 compaction + eviction-kernel backoff on a 5% traffic slice, run for 2h, collect metrics: paging_io, fragmentation, kv_reuse_rate, p99 latency.
alice: running the canary now. also enabling tenant-level sampler to trace the top 20 longctx sessions and their page footprints.
kv-bot: canary launched: canary_id=canary-jupiter-1958001308, nodes=3, start=1958001310
carlos: nice. if results are promising we should add a fairshare knob that proactively lowers residency allowance for tenants that cause high fragmentation + low reuse. basically a composite score.
dana: agreed. but be careful: some telemetry-heavy tenants will look bad but are important customers. we need a safe rollback and explicit SRE/CS alert ahead of enforcement.
ben: right — implement enforcement via soft shaper first (throttle generation speed), then hard eviction cap if soft fails. also emit reasons in audit logs.
emma: snapshot after 30m: paging_io -18%, fragmentation -0.06, reuse_rate +0.11, p99 latency +0.8% (within SLO). looks promising.
alice: great. log dump shows a few longctx sessions still hoarding pages — sampling trace: session-id=abc123 walked 2.1M keys over 9k tokens, created many ephemeral pages. we'll add route-level back-pressure for sequences >8k tokens.
carlos: final ask: please add an integration test that simulates mixed tenants (one noisy longctx, many small) and measures residency fairness. add to perf-regressions suite.
dana: putting a PR together with compaction toggle + kernel backoff + sampler traces. i'll tag infra and cs for rollout plan.
alice: thanks all. follow-up in #eng-runtime tomorrow with aggregated charts. :party:
